run_2_incremental_pair.purpose: CR3/CR4/CR5 -- crawl 1 full explore + build_portal_persona, crawl 2 incremental against the byte-identical site

crawl_1.note: full crawl, all 9 fixture screens reached

crawl_2.stop_reason: frontier empty -- 1 screen(s) skipped as unchanged since the stored persona, and so NOT explored on this crawl

run_2_incremental_pair.bug: ISS-t165-crawl-traversal-3 (filed by check A): the incremental crawl's frontier is seeded only from base_url via _seed(); the only place a node ever enters rt.frontier.queue is _enqueue(), reachable only from try_action() -> _click_loop() -> visit_node(). explore_incremental.skip_unchanged() short-circuits BEFORE visit_node() runs, so a skipped node's children are never enqueued this crawl. Crawl 2's own graph therefore contains exactly 1 node (the skipped entry screen). Its stop_reason starts with 'frontier empty', which every caller treats as frontier_exhausted=True (confirmed against explore.py's own _bfs queue-drain logic), so persona_changes.classify() is invoked with frontier_exhausted=True and reports the other 8 previously-known, byte-identical, never-removed screens as missing_screens -- not missing_unjudged. This is a direct violation of D-040 acceptance test (c): 'the same two crawls with nothing removed produce zero missing entries.' It reproduces on the mainline incremental path (not a corner case) and is not caught by any existing test, because no test combines a real incremental crawl's own graph with persona_changes.classify() -- tests/test_persona_changes.py uses synthetic fixtures only, and the incremental_pair fixture in tests/test_explore_completeness.py never calls classify() on its own crawl-2 output.

terminal_status_login_branch_check.method: static read of src/autotester/stages/explore_status.py::terminal_status, confirmed structurally rather than by a login fixture crawl
terminal_status_login_branch_check.finding: CrawlStatus.COMPLETED is returned from exactly one place: the final else branch, itself only reached when `if not completed` is false. LOGIN_FAILED and LOGIN_WALL are returned from earlier branches that return before that point. There is no route by which a login-branch return can produce a COMPLETED reading; the two statuses are mutually exclusive by construction, not by convention.
terminal_status_login_branch_check.conclusion: NO laundering route found via terminal_status. Did not find a way to make a crawl claim completed on an unexhausted frontier through this function.
